full_judgment:
3. It is admitted by the learned Counsel for the petitioner Mr Azizul Hoque that already issues have been framed in the suit by the trial Court including the issues on the point of res judicata in view of the pleadings of the parties. No counter affidavit as I see has been filed by the opposite parties in this Rule to deny the facts of the Rule petition. However, it is question of law whether the instant suit shall proceed or its plaint shall be rejected on the ground of res judicata as contemplated under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The contention of the defendant-petitioner is that on the same subject matter previously Other Class Suit 461 of 1978 was filed in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi by the defendant 1 and that suit has been decreed on 11-8-1979 in favour of the defendant 1. But it has not been stated what was the nature of that suit. The trial Court has found that the said decree was an ex parte decree and the plaintiffs of the present suit were not impleaded as party in that suit. It has also been mentioned in the application that defendant 5 had filed another suit being Other Class Suit 159 of 1979 which was dismissed for default on 30-5-79 by the Munsif, Natore. There are no averments as to the nature of that suit also in the application for rejection of the plaint. The trial Court has passed the impugned order discussing the relevant points elaborately and found that the results of neither of those two suits as mentioned above has affected the present plaintiffs locus standi to file the present suit and its cause of action. 

 Admittedly, in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, the present plaintiffs were not parties in the former suit which was decreed ex parte and the subsequent suit was dismissed for default. It is not clear what was the nature of those two suits. To bring the case within the ambit of section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as I understand, the issues in the former suit and the subsequent suit shall be the same, the suit should be between the same parties and the subject-matter should be the same and the former suit should be finally decided.
